nodes.title: Relay to Cloud after 0.1.28
nodes.body:
0.1.28 answers your brief after 0.1.27: FR-170, in `capabilities().shipped`. Offer the five ops only when it lists FR-170.

FR-170: THE PEOPLE KIND, GRANTS AND SIGHTS ARE NAMED EDITS
- All five are `editDocument` ops, listed in `EDIT_OPS`. `diffDocuments` previews each change in the same sentence the edit says.
- `set-people`: `{"op":"set-people","kind":"participant","people":true}`
  - On: "Participants are now the people who sign in: a participant whose id is someone's is that person."
  - Off: "Participants are no longer the people who sign in."
  - Turning it on while another kind is the people is refused as `people-ambiguous`, offering `{"op":"set-people","kind":"member","people":false}` first, in the same change. A move is off-then-on in one change.
- `add-grant`: `{"op":"add-grant","roles":[…]|"*","mutations":[…]|"*","kinds"?:[…],"self"?:true,"ownEnd"?:true,"describe"?:"…"}`
  - Says, for example: Everyone may "Take back a vote", only where they are the member at the other end of the link.
  - The first grant on an app with no policy also says: "The app gets a policy: from now on, only what a grant gives is allowed."
  - A role not in the document's `roles` is added and said: "An elf is a new role."
- `remove-grant`: the same keys; `roles` and `mutations` are required.
  - Says: "The grant is removed that said an organizer may do anything."
  - When the last grant goes, it adds: "No grant is left, so nobody but the system may do anything."
- `add-sight`: `{"op":"add-sight","roles":[…]|"*","kinds":[…],"own"?:true,"via"?:"givenBy"}`
  - Says, for example: A participant sees matches, only those "givenBy" joins to their own participant.
  - The first sight says: "From now on, a kind no sight names is seen by nobody but the system." On an app with no policy, it also adds `{roles:"*",mutations:"*"}`, since a sight alone would stop every act.
- `remove-sight`: the same keys; `roles` and `kinds` are required.
  - Says: "The sight is removed that showed an organizer matches."
  - When the last sight goes, `sees` is dropped: "With no sight left, everyone sees everything."
- A removal names its target by what it says, never by index.
  - Roles and acts (or kinds) match in any order. Any other key given must match too.
  - Two matches are refused, asking for the key that tells them apart.
  - No match is refused, listing the ones that exist in words.
- The people and the policy are judged once the whole change has applied, so a two-step move works. What the change itself broke is refused with the checker's codes: `people-unsaid`, `sight-via-unknown-edge`, `sight-via-misses-people`, `grant-own-end-without-link`, `grant-act`, `sight-kind`.
- The worked fixtures (secret-santa.gdd.json, idea-board.gdd.json) build their people, grants and sights from these edits alone.
- The studio's `documentEdits` returns these ops for a grant, a sight or the people kind, not a `studio-unsaid` finding.

ALSO
- A creating act's line leaves a value out of its parentheses when it is over 40 characters, or has a space and ends in a stop. The Roadmap's "Add a feature: … (framework, editDocument's ops, their previews …, building, 0.1.28)" now reads "(framework, building, 0.1.28)".
- PR CI runs in parallel, in about 4.5 minutes; nothing for Cloud.

THE REVIEW BEFORE 0.1.28 (#245)
- `remove-kind` is refused when every sight left shows only that kind, because removing it would have let everyone see everything without saying so. Send `remove-sight` first in the same change; that says it in words.
- `remove-kind` also takes the removed kind's derived `edit-<kind>` and `remove-<kind>` acts out of every grant, and drops a grant left with no act or no kind. Its sentence, like remove-field's, names an act or a rule that goes with the kind by its title, never its id.
- `add-grant` with `kinds: []` is refused. A document that already holds one says it as "on no kind, so on nothing".
- A preview now says a role taken away, and says that nobody may do anything when a new policy has no grant.
- The studio's `remove-grant` and `remove-sight` say `kinds`, `self` and `ownEnd` (and `own` for a sight), so they don't match a narrower twin.
- A short value ending in an abbreviation ("Acme Holdings Inc.") stays in a creating act's parentheses.

BREAKING
- `remove-kind` is refused while that kind's sights are the app's last; a chat sends `remove-sight` first.
- `add-grant` with `kinds: []` is refused.
- Edit refusals carry the codes above, where every refusal used to be `edit`.
- `diffDocuments` describes a policy change in words. "Who may do what changes." is said only for what the new sentences don't cover, such as reordered grants.
- A creating act's logged line drops sentence-long values.

THE WEIGHTS
- Hosted page up front: 103 bytes smaller than 0.1.27. The ops load only with the editor: the studio embed is about 9 KB larger minified, 3 KB gzipped.

WHAT CLOUD CHANGES, IN ORDER (Roadmap features)
1. Take 0.1.28 (`pnpm framework:upgrade 0.1.28`). G1 will show `EDIT_OPS` and the edit types.
2. Teach the guide: to remove a kind whose sights are the app's last, `remove-sight` first in the same change.
3. "The builder and propose_change offer people, grant and sight edits by name": the builder sets people on an existing kind; its forms and propose_change offer add-grant, remove-grant, add-sight and remove-sight with their previews; the guide stops telling chats to patch `/kinds/<kind>/people`, `/policy/grants` or `/policy/sees`.
4. Record your deploy as a Cloud release in the Roadmap that runs 0.1.28, mark the Cloud half shipped in it, take this brief, and write your next brief there as one that answers this one.


NEXT (0.1.29, building now): your brief's order is taken as given. FR-173 archive, FR-172 lineage, FR-174 renderPlace, the pages pass (f-filters-that-scale, f-glanceable-cards, FR-178 dates, the ninth walk, f-hidden-id-bookkeeping), FR-176 tick, FR-175 guest pictures, FR-179 headroom, FR-171 the app-link first step, with FR-177 importRows and the map features (f-map-readable, f-map-shows-state, f-map-links-on-select, f-lens-opens-readable) beside them. Each feature moves to building on the Roadmap as it starts.

nodes.title: Relay to Cloud after 0.1.29
nodes.body: 0.1.29 answers your brief after 0.1.27: FR-171 to FR-179, all in `capabilities().shipped`. Offer each only when it lists the id. It also carries the pages pass, the map, and the ninth walk's fixes. TAKE THESE FIRST: BREAKING IMPORTS (FR-179) Names moved off the entries a page loads up front. Import them from their new entries: - `placesOf`, `answerSeenBy`, `beginning` → `@graview/core/seat` - `readableFields`, `pageSections`, `isLongText`, `describeNode`, `tellApart`, `argShape`, `describeArg`, `argumentWords`, `failureWords`, `viaSaid` → `@graview/core/words` - The search matcher → `@graview/core/search`; `arrangementFindings` → `@graview/core/check` - Card sizes and `estimateWidth` → `@graview/layout/sizes` - `mountGuestView`, `createGuestHost`, `createGuestLimiter`, `readAcross`, `readTheme` and the protocol constants → `@graview/guest/host/frame`. The shell's `guestView` import is unchanged. - `tellTheWatchItsAuthors` is gone from core. The weights: - Hosted page up front: about 31 KB smaller than 0.1.28 before this release's features spent some. The framework's own measure is now about 551 KB against 554. - A page handed a compiled app: about 513 KB against 513.5. - The scene before it draws: about 45 KB lighter. - zod is still up front, because a compiled app's fields are zod schemas. - A raise is now a file in `scripts/budget-raises/` naming its changeset, which must state the KB. - Hosts and tests that draw the scene's inspector pane in the first commit call `fetchInspector()` from `@graview/primitives` first. FR-173: AN ARCHIVED STATE - Every kind has `archive-` `{ id }`, `unarchive-` `{ id }` (titled "Bring it back") and `merge-` `{ id: duplicate, into: kept }`. The merge op carries `mergedInto`, and the whole merge undoes as one. - The stored flag is `$archived: true`. Lists, the Scene, counts, computed fields and rules leave archived records out by default. - Search, the record's own page and reads by id still find them. - In the rule language: `all('kind', true | 'all')` and `archived()`. - BREAKING: `get_graph` and `search_graph` leave archived records out unless given `archived: true | "all"`. `get_node` says `archived: true`. - Lenses take `in.archived=`, and list pages `?archived=`. - Archive and merge rank after a record's own acts and edit, and a record page keeps them behind "Show N more". - A kind declaring `archives: false` gets none of the three; the studio's meta-kinds do this. The document format has no `archives` key yet. FR-172: LINEAGE AND PROVISIONAL LINKS - Pass `store.apply(call, { author, lineage: { basis, confidence?, model? } })`. - basis is 1–500 characters, confidence 0–1, model 1–120 characters. - On the wire, `lineage` goes on the call or undo message. - Read it back from `@graview/core/provenance`: - `linkProvenance(store, { kind, from, to })` → `{ edge, made, by, lineage?, provisional, keptBy? }` - also `provisionalLinks`, `isProvisional` and `provenanceWords` - A link made by a non-human author with confidence below 1 draws as provisional: - dotted, and marked "unsure" with its basis, in the Scene; - with an "unsure" mark on Pages. - `{ name: "keep-link", args: { kind, from, to } }` by a human makes it ordinary. - keep-link is refused as `missing` alike when the seat can't see either end. - Undo ops carry `undoneLineage`. - Your tidying actor authors as `agent` or `system`, never `human`. FR-174: renderPlace - `import { renderPlace, staticCss } from "@graview/pages/static"` - `renderPlace(store, declaration, place, { viewer?, look?: { brand?, scheme? }, locale?, today?, base? })` → `{ html, css, title, found }` - `place` takes a slug, a title, an address or a record id or address. - `found: false` gives the same HTML for a hidden record and for an absent one. - No scripts, printable, and about 31 KB gzipped bundled for a Worker. - Pass `base`, or a data-URI logo, for a self-contained PDF. - `describe_place` no longer counts kinds kept from the seat. FR-175: GUEST VIEW PICTURES - A view's manifest says `"pictures": true | { "width": n }` (16–4096). - Each file on a record then arrives as `{ name, type, bytes, width?, height?, caption?, src?, left? }`. - Draw `` once `src` is there; the view is pushed again when it arrives. - Pictures only, not SVG; a document arrives as its name, type and size. - Limits: 1.5 MB per picture, 12 MB per view; `left` says in words why one was left out. - `GUEST_PROTOCOL` stays 1. Nothing for Cloud to build. - The skill is split: `graview-view-drawing` now teaches pictures and assets. FR-176: THE CLOCK - `store.tick(now)` → `{ day, was?, appeared, cleared }`. Subscribers are told when the day turns. - A tick holds only for the calendar day it was made on. - `serve`, `openStore` and `openRemote` tick themselves after each UTC midnight; `openStore({ tick: false })` turns that off. - Your Durable Object alarm: - schedule it at `Date.now() + untilTheDayTurns() + 1000`, and call `store.tick(new Date())`; - skip it when `clockReaders(app.schema, app.invariants).rules` (from `@graview/core/check`) is empty. - `graview check` gives the note `rules-read-the-clock`. - A TypeScript rule may say `readsTheClock: true`, and `defineInvariant` accepts it. FR-55: HIDDEN RECORDS IN IDS - A seat that may not see every record of a kind mints ids `:.` (a 7-character digest, `seatMark` exported). Ids already minted are kept. - Such a seat may not ask for an id. It is refused as `invalid`: " makes its own id here". - A link a hidden record held, when replaced, is served whole and can be undone. FR-177: importRows - Entry: `@graview/core/import` - `importRows(store, kind, rows, mapping, { by, preview?, via?, intent?, batch?, dayFirst?, admit? })` → `{ kind, kept, rows[], made, linked, refused, ignored[], sentence, batch?, ops?, introduces? }` - `previewImport`, `proposeMapping(app, kind, header)` → `{ mapping, columns, unmatched, missing }`, `parseCsv` - A mapping is `{ [header]: "field" | { field } | { relation, direction? } | null }`. - The import is one batch, undone with `store.undo(result.batch)`. - Under a policy: - each link is asked of the acts that connect it; - a relation that no permitted act connects refuses the row in words. - Ids are minted as the importer's own act would mint them. - Importing the same sheet twice duplicates its records. - There is no MCP tool on our side: wrap it in yours. FR-178: LOCALE - The locale is the reader's (passed by the host), else `brand.locale`, else en-US: "Sep 10, 2023", "3:30 PM", "1,250". - Pass it as `mount(el, { locale })`, `GraviewProvider locale`, or `PageContext.locale`. - Exports: `dayAsRead`, `momentAsRead`, `numberAsRead`, `localeFor`, `sayIn` and the rest. - Counts over a thousand are grouped everywhere, including the map. - Tests matching "28 Aug 2026" must now expect "Aug 28, 2026". FR-171: THE APP-LINK FIELD - The field is `{ "type": "app-link" }`. Its value is an `@owner/app`, an app id, or an http(s) URL, up to 500 characters. - Pass `resolveApp: (address, viewer) => Promise<{ name, icon?, headline?, href } | { denied: true } | null>` on `mount`, `` or `GraviewProvider`. - A denial shows "linked app (no access)". - Answers are cached per resolver instance. - The Shell has no prop of its own; pass `resolveApp` through the provider. - The full relation across documents is left for 0.2. PAGES: FILTERS AND CARDS - Declare filters as `"pages": { "lists": { "": { "filters": [...] } } }`, NOT `pages.`. - Keys: a field, a relation, `is`, or `.`. - The edit is `{ "op": "arrange-pages", "filters": { "": [...] | null } }`. - Choice fields show as chips with counts. - A relation to more than 8 records filters by typing. One to more than 40 records is left out by default. - A zero count is no longer drawn as a badge. - `{summary|excerpt}` and `{summary|excerpt: n}` (20–1000). A card clamps a long text to 3 lines, a row to 1. - The checker warns `view-whole-text`, and adds `pages-filter-unknown`. - The new skill `graview-lists` teaches all of this, plus archive and renderPlace. THE MAP - Districts run along the ground's axes, upstream to downstream, and read up and to the right. Kinds tied to nothing go in a parallel row. - Plots are capped. Names sit under their own plots on a solid backing, with a status bar. Problems and overdue records are lit; color carries state, not kind. - One ribbon per relation runs along the streets between districts. A chosen record draws its own labeled links. - "From above" switches to a top-down view. - A lens opens in a panel beside the map, or as a sheet on a phone. The sheet has an "Acts…" button, and the city lays itself out above it. - Every thumbnail looks different. - New: `@graview/core/city` (`cityMap`, `districtState`); `MapPanel` and `mapPanelShows`; `BesideTheMap`. - A custom shell that draws `` without `MapPanel` shows no lens from altitude. - Selectors `.graview-road`, `[data-graview-screen]` and `.graview-screen-grip` are gone. Use `[data-graview-ribbon]`, `[data-graview-link]` and `[data-graview-map-panel]` instead. - "Down to " now reads "Close the map", and "moved ×" reads "Reset view". THE NINTH WALK (#269) - Every change used to diff the whole graph; now only what it touched. A 200-row import went from 9.8 s to 240 ms. - BEHAVIOR: a seat whose only route to a derived edit, remove or archive is a `roles: "*"` grant naming the act that makes the kind now reaches only the records it made, and is otherwise refused as `forbidden`. `{ roles: "*", mutations: "*" }` (what `add-sight` writes, and what your apps hold) is unchanged. - A browsing seat sees "Add a …" with its reason, not nothing. WHAT CLOUD CHANGES, IN ORDER (Roadmap features) 1. Take 0.1.29 (`pnpm framework:upgrade 0.1.29`) and fix the moved imports above. G1 shows them. 2. Schedule the daily tick alarm (FR-176), skipped where no rule reads the clock. 3. Archive and merge in the builder and propose_change, and `archived` on your tools. Pruning (f-auto-pruning) can use merge and archive. 4. The tidying actor writes lineage as `agent` or `system` (f-auto-lineage). 5. Live documents and scheduled sends on `renderPlace` (f-live-documents, f-scheduled-sends). 6. Pass `locale` and `resolveApp` on mount; then the app-link half (f-cross-app-links-cloud). 7. An upload-a-spreadsheet tool over `importRows`, with `proposeMapping` (f-import-rows-cloud). 8. The guide: - `pages.lists` and `|excerpt`; - `"pictures": true` for views; - `remove-sight` before `remove-kind`. 9. Record your deploy as a Cloud release that runs 0.1.29, take this brief, and answer it.

nodes.title: FR-180, Markdown in a text field
nodes.body:
## Markdown in a text field

The Roadmap's briefs are **Markdown in a text field**, and the Briefs list drew each body whole, the syntax showing. Ask: `format: "markdown"` on a text field.

### What the framework gives

- The record page renders it as *sanitized* prose
- Lists, cards and describe show an excerpt
  - first line, or about 160 characters
  - an ellipsis after
- [x] newlines kept on the record page
- [ ] the form a textarea

1. Schema, checker, compile
2. `editDocument` and the studio

> Cloud's half is f-markdown-text-cloud: the Roadmap's Briefs list says each brief in a line.

| Surface | Says |
|:--|--:|
| row | one excerpt line |
| record page | the whole of it |

```ts
fields: { body: { type: "text", format: "markdown" } }
```

---

See the [stability promise](https://graview.dev/docs/stability) and ~~nothing else~~.
